_why: J23: `exec` verdict recovery used to grep the WHOLE transcript. `codex exec ... -` echoes the piped prompt into that transcript, and a dispatch prompt states its output contract by listing the legal STATUS values one per line (references/codex-implementer-prompt.md requires it), so on a dispatch that never ran `tail -1` returned the LAST option of our own contract block -- deterministically `STATUS: NEEDS_CONTEXT`. The caller then wrote it to --out, where h_mad_extract_verdict.py accepts it without complaint. Silence would have been safer; that path manufactured confidence. Measured on a real 401-auth failure: the only four STATUS lines in a 20,770-byte log were the prompt's own, at 268/271/274/277. The sibling defect in the same recovery block reported `tree delta: 1 changed` for a subdirectory that was clean, because `git -C <subdir> status --porcelain` with no pathspec reports the entire work tree.
_provenance: Both guards shipped with unit tests and NO mutation spec. Measured 2026-09-02: 39 specs existed and none named `_verdict_after_boundary` or the porcelain pathspec, so nothing proved those seven assertions bind. That is the gap the exec-verdict-laundering brief left as `mutation-verify both guards` -- the answer is that it was never done, not that no spec could be found by name.

mutations.name: recovery-scans-the-whole-transcript
mutations._mechanism: The original defect exactly. Ignore where the boundary was found and start at line 0, so the scan sees our own echoed contract block again and `tail -1` returns its last option.

mutations.name: missing-boundary-does-not-refuse-on-codex
mutations._mechanism: A TRUNCATED echo can still carry the contract block while losing the trailing boundary. Dropping the codex-arm refusal reopens the defect on exactly that case, which is the one where the agent is least likely to have written anything.

mutations.name: slices-past-the-FIRST-boundary
mutations._mechanism: `tail -1` picks the LAST occurrence. With `head -1` the scan resumes after the first, so anything between two boundaries -- our echoed prompt included, on a redispatch appending to the same log -- is back in range.

mutations.name: tree-delta-drops-the-pathspec
mutations._mechanism: `git -C <subdir> status --porcelain` with no pathspec reports the whole work tree, so a clean --cd subdir is reported as changed and the caller reads work that did not happen. `-- .` is the entire guard.

mutations.name: agy-fallback-ignores-the-pre-dispatch-floor
mutations._mechanism: The agy arm has no boundary to expect, so it cannot refuse the way the codex arm does -- the pre_lines floor is its whole guard. Drop it and a codex dispatch whose echo was truncated before its boundary landed leaves a contract block that a later agy dispatch on the same --log scans whole, laundering NEEDS_CONTEXT into --out. Reached through the other arm; both append with `>>`.
